purpose: Qualify ordinary hosted pipeline values in object/dictionary literals through existing native success capture; emission is separate from execution.

validation.independentReview: One fresh read-only literal_pipeline_value_review pass found no actionable P0-P3 defects. Admission/capability guards, object/dictionary construction and property order, lowering, whole-pipeline capture in active scope, partial-output and error owner inspected. Fixture hash/license/attributes verified; no tests run or remote-source comparison by reviewer.
limits: Ordinary qualified pipelines in literal values remain hosted while surrounding literal construction is compiled. This is not direct CLR translation of ForEach-Object or arbitrary pipeline commands.

Proof uses offline Invoke-RestMethod and clock functions, explicitly loaded utility/management modules, and disabled module autoload. Actual HTTP/ARIN, complete module execution and all IPv4 validation failures are unqualified.

Typed invocation continuations and Out-Null retain conservative wrapper/statement ownership and may emit wrapper methods without native binding. Redirection/background and runtime-free Strict gain no admission from this rule.

New direct differential cases cover ForEach-Object pipelines, cardinality, local state, order, partial failure/source positions and finally. Every other command or stream combination is not newly qualified.

Same-input full five-packet comparison is net10.0 only; focused generated modules execute on Windows PowerShell 5.1/net472 and PowerShell 7/net10.0. No other platform, performance, package or release proof.

Exploratory runs failed on a test Count compilation error, missing ConvertTo-Json after disabling autoload, and incorrectly treating conservative wrapper emission as native admission. Corrected probes passed; production source remained unchanged throughout.
